<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a54e2b2657ed309081dcace045fa569e2f44c264` — the merge of head `1eada1f13463e3a58ba733ea2ee652893ed59e90` into base `013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a54e2b2657ed309081dcace045fa569e2f44c264 && git checkout a54e2b2657ed309081dcace045fa569e2f44c264
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260 1eada1f13463e3a58ba733ea2ee652893ed59e90 && git checkout -B drift-repro 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260 && git merge --no-ff 1eada1f13463e3a58ba733ea2ee652893ed59e90

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 013f97df93ed66d0aeec45ec1d507da303991260` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1eada1f13463e3a58ba733ea2ee652893ed59e90`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20701 body and all twenty-two comments (governing: triage's first direction `5897601448`, triage's answer `5920419144` (Ask 1 folded in as REST item 5; Ask 2: the preview does not detect drift), the seat's claim `5920542737`, the newest `os-dev-report` `5921008893`; context: PR #20941 landed as `f80e2a6dad` and its record `5919882310`); PR #20956 body, file list (4 files: `packages/rest/src/import-runner.ts` +63/-16, `packages/rest/src/import-row-schema-drift-20701.test.ts` +117/-39, `.changeset/20701-import-row-not-null-and-unique-door-answer.md` new, `.changeset/20701-import-row-schema-drift-door-answer.md` +1/-2) and the net diff `75519e1c0a...1eada1f134` (208 insertions, 57 deletions, one commit); the check-runs on the head, polled to convergence; the `Check Changeset` job log. Source premises (`error-response.ts`, `import-runner.ts`, `engine.ts`, `duplicate-record-error.ts`, `unique-violation.ts`, `record-validator.ts`, `quickjs-runner.ts`, ADR-0112, ADR-0113, `check-empty-changeset.mjs`, the three `20701` changesets) were read at the PR head by `git show`; nothing was built, run, checked out or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The widened gate is item 4's gate, adopting the door's verdict; no second rule is added.** `toFailedResult` still asks `mapDataError(err, objectName)` only when the thrown error carries no finding, and `adoptDoorVerdict` takes the door's body whole when `door.code` is in `ADOPTED_DOOR_VERDICTS`; the import derives nothing about the error: which arm fired, the `field` and the sentence are all the mapper's. The one condition added, "a `VALIDATION_FAILED` with no finding is not taken", decides whether to adopt, never what the error is, and it keeps the old answer for an empty or bare-name `fields` (a control, not a classification). The one thing the import does to the door's body is its own pre-existing rendering rule, a finding wins over the top-level code (#4633), applied to the door's finding as it already is to the engine's. So triage's "the same gate as item 4" (`5920419144`) holds. Every class that can now reach a row through the two new verdicts, read from the mapper's arm order at the head:

- `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, three producers of that verdict:
  1. The structured 409 arm (`code === 'DUPLICATE_RECORD' && name === 'DuplicateRecordError'`): the engine's envelope, which every engine driver exit raises (`envelopeUniqueViolation` at `createWithAutonumberResync` both exits, `insert`'s batch `bulkCreate` catch, `update` by id, `updateMany`; `insertMany` delegates to `insert` with `__partialRowErrors`, so the bulk path is the same catch). Before: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` (via `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope`), `field` = the envelope's, `error` = the engine's sentence. After: same `code`, same `field` (the arm reads the same `error.field`), the door's sentence. Answers what the door answers; pinned on insert (`POST` door), upsert-update (`PATCH` door) and the async job.
  2. The `isUniqueViolationError` branch: a raw driver refusal without the envelope (code `23505`/`ER_DUP_ENTRY`/`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE`/`UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, errno 1062, the message regex, or the same on a `cause` up to four deep), when it declares no status and is not sandbox-origin. Before: the DIALECT code on the wire `code`, no `field`, the runner's own conflict sentence. After: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, `field` from `uniqueViolationColumn` (message, `detail`, `cause`), the door's sentence. The right direction and the door's answer; on the engine this shape is unreachable (the five exits above), so it needs a non-engine protocol to occur. The dev's note is right.
  3. The sandbox unwrap door: a QuickJS body throwing the registered `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` (kept by `thrownCodeFields`) with a declared status under 500 or none. Before: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, no `field`, the QuickJS debug wrapper as the sentence. After: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, no `field`, the body's `innerMessage`. The door's answer, and the same residue class item 4's record named for `INVALID_FIELD`; unmeasured, not in the changeset.
  4. The declared-status 4xx passthrough: a non-sandbox producer throwing `{ code: 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION', status: 4xx }`. Before: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, the producer's own `field` if it set one, the runner's sentence. After: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, no `field` (the passthrough carries none), the message with a `CODE:` prefix stripped and a 500-character bound instead of 300. A producer-set `field` is dropped, as the door drops it; no producer of that shape reaches the import through the engine (driver-memory's raw refusal is enveloped at the exits above). Noted by the dev; a residue, not a verdict mover. A producer that merely speaks `DUPLICATE_RECORD` keeps its code (not in the set; `import-runner-unique-violation-row` GUARD, still green), unless its message matches the shared predicate, in which case the door already said `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` and the row now agrees.
- `VALIDATION_FAILED` with a finding, two producers of that verdict:
  1. The structured arm (`code === 'VALIDATION_FAILED' || name === 'ValidationError'`) copies the error's own `fields`. Adoption needs `fields[0]` to be an object, but that is exactly `first` in `toFailedResult`, already defined, so the door is never asked. By construction this arm can never be adopted: the engine's `ValidationError`, a sandboxed `VALIDATION_FAILED` with findings, and any producer with object findings keep the finding-wins path unchanged; an empty, absent or bare-string `fields` is not taken and keeps the old rule. Unchanged.
  2. The driver-text NOT NULL branch: reached only by an error that clears every arm above it (no sandbox crash, no structured code, not `PERMISSION_DENIED`, no `innerMessage`, no declared status, not a unique violation, not the sandbox wrapper, not `EnvironmentKernelFactory`, not `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, no missing-column match) and whose message matches SQLite `NOT NULL constraint failed: t.c`, Postgres `null value in column "c"` or MySQL `Column 'c' cannot be null`. That is the driver's own refusal, rethrown unchanged by the engine (`update`'s docblock: "Every other driver failure is rethrown UNCHANGED, a NOT NULL violation"; `envelopeUniqueViolation` returns a non-unique error as is; the engine's redaction touches the log slot only). Before: the dialect code (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL`; `23502`, `ER_BAD_NULL_ERROR` on the other dialects), no `field`, and a readable sentence on SQLite only (`sanitizeRowError`'s NOT NULL regex is SQLite-shaped; on Postgres and MySQL the SQL backstop shipped the driver's trailing reason verbatim, relation name included). After: `code: 'required'`, `field`, "c is required" on all three dialects. Not reclassified: it is the condition the door already classifies this way, and no other error class carries that text without also carrying a status or an `innerMessage` that an earlier arm takes.
- Triage's ⛔ (no driver dialect's code on the wire `code`) holds for both new verdicts: `adoptDoorVerdict`'s `code` is the finding's (`required`, a member of the field-level catalog the row already speaks) or the door's top-level code, and every arm that can put one of the three adopted values there either hard-codes the member or passes it through `thrownCodeFields`, which demotes an unregistered spelling to `declaredCode` (and such a body is then not in the set). Pinned on every new case by `DIALECT_CODE` (`/^(SQLITE_|ER_)|^\d{5}$/`). Residue outside item 5: the non-adopted fallthrough still relays `e?.code` for other driver refusals (a FOREIGN KEY or CHECK failure), which the door answers as a sanitised fault; pre-existing, outside this claim (③).
- The upsert's match lookup (`findExisting` via `findData`) is a read and can raise neither verdict (its `INVALID_FIELD` case is item 4's, unchanged); the reference resolver swallows every throw; `coerceRow`'s cell failures never reach `toFailedResult`; `previewVerdict` runs on the dry run only and asks `validateData`, which performs no driver write. So the dry run is untouched, as measured and as the pin file's docblock declines to vouch for.

**(b) `code: 'required'` on the NOT NULL row is the row's own convention, and it answers triage's sentence literally.** `import-integration.test.ts` "required-field dry-run fidelity" pins a metadata-`required` field as `{ field: 'status', code: 'required' }` on the dry run and on the commit alike, while `POST /data/:object` answers that same refusal as top-level `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the finding: the row has always rendered a `VALIDATION_FAILED` plus finding as the finding's `code` and `field` (#4633, the ADR-0114 field-level catalog), and `VALIDATION_FAILED` reaches a row only when no finding names a field. Applying that rule to the door's synthesized finding gives `required` and `must` with the door's sentence; carrying `VALIDATION_FAILED` instead would have made a driver NOT NULL row read differently from a metadata-required row for the same user-visible condition, and would have broken the row's convention. It "disagrees" with the door's top-level `code` exactly as every existing finding row does. Triage's "answers the door's `required` finding, naming the field" is met: the finding, the field, the door's sentence. One difference worth naming, not a defect of this item: the engine's own required refusal renders the field's LABEL ("Status is required", #3957) while the door's NOT NULL sentence uses the API name ("must is required"), since the mapper reads the driver text and has no label; the row matches the door, which is what the card asks.

**(c) Unique-conflict row: nothing a caller relied on is lost, and `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope` is dead in practice.** `code` and `field` are unchanged (pinned, and the envelope's `field` is the same value the arm reads). What moves is the prose: the engine's "Duplicate record refused on 'obj': a unique constraint on 'f' already holds this value. No record was written." becomes "A record with this f already exists". The object name is the import's own object, and "no record was written" is `ok: false` / `action: 'failed'` on the same row. `developerMessage` was never on the row (not a key of `ImportRowResultSchema`); the row carried the envelope's `message`, which is what the door ships as `developerMessage`, so no channel disappears, only a sentence changes. No pin relied on the engine's sentence on a row (`import-runner-unique-violation-row` pins `code`, and the producer case its own message; both green). The runner's own `UNNAMED_CONFLICT` docblock already declares the row's conflict wording to be "the same wording `mapDataError` puts in the 409 body"; the #14095 envelope had displaced that with the engine's message, so this PR restores the runner's stated intent. Cosmetic residue: `sanitizeRowError` still spells "already exists." with a trailing period where the door has none, on a path now unreachable through the door. The dev's note on `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope` is right: after this PR it can change the answer only when the error is the engine's envelope AND `fields[0]` is an object whose `code` is nullish (otherwise the door's 409 arm answers first, or the finding wins); `DuplicateRecordError` declares no `fields`. Dead, harmless, and left in place for the door-parity docblock it is named in.

**(d) The deliberate correction, confirmed; and the new changeset is accurate.**
- Corrected note: `.changeset/20701-import-row-schema-drift-door-answer.md`, item 4's (PR #20941). It is pending: at the head `packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md` carries none of its text (0 occurrences of the removed sentence), `@objectstack/rest` is at `17.5.0`, and all three `20701` changesets are still in `.changeset/`.
- Removed sentence, quoted whole: "Rows for a unique conflict or a NOT NULL failure are unchanged."
- Does this PR make it false? Yes. The NOT NULL row moves on `code` (a dialect code to `required`), gains `field`, and changes its sentence; the unique-conflict row's sentence moves from the engine's to the door's. Both notes are `@objectstack/rest` `patch` and pending, so `changeset version` would compile them into one CHANGELOG entry in which that sentence contradicts the note beside it. Removing it is the right correction (the new note states the change); the edit is that one sentence plus a re-wrap of the neighbouring line, nothing else.
- Every remaining sentence of that note, judged at the head: (1) the title "fix(rest): an import row for a missing database column answers what the create door answers (#20701)": still true. (2) "When an object declares a field whose database column is missing (the schema has drifted from the metadata), a committed row that writes that field now fails with `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`, `field` set to the field, and the sentence `POST /api/v1/data/:object` gives for the same key: ...": still true; an `INVALID_FIELD` body carries no finding, so `adoptDoorVerdict` yields `code = door.code`, `field = door.field`, `error = door.error`, byte-identical to item 4's literal, and the drift pins are retained as controls. (3) "It used to fail with the database's own code and text (for example `SQLITE_ERROR` and `table X has no column named f`) and no `field`.": still true, history. (4) "The async job's rows, read from `GET /api/v1/data/import/jobs/:jobId/results`, change the same way.": still true. (5) "The row now classifies a write error through the same mapper as the create door, and takes that answer when it is `INVALID_FIELD`.": still true; it now also takes two more verdicts, which the new note states, so the pair reads whole without contradiction (no longer exhaustive, not false). (6) "The dry run still cannot see a missing column, because it checks the metadata and not the table, so it previews such a row as `ok`.": still true, the dry run is untouched. The sibling pending note `20701-import-row-field-and-missing-column-wording.md` (items 2 and 3) was read as well: its "A unique conflict row now names its column too ... as the `409` does" stays true (`field` unchanged); nothing in it is touched.
- The gate: `Check Changeset` is `check-empty-changeset.mjs` naming exactly that file ("present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR") with the two-class text, whose DELIBERATE CORRECTION remedy is "do NOT restore it; say so on the PR and get it confirmed". The PR body's section "A pending release note corrected: please confirm" says so. Under `landing-operations.md` (the DELIBERATE CORRECTION red is confirmed by a same-head at-tier PASS record that names the corrected note and judges it sentence by sentence), this section is that confirmation. The by-design red then rides into the queue only under SKILL.md's three conditions (declared by design on the pushed branch; the gate does not run on `merge_group`; the PR comment names the gate and the cause), which the dispatching seat verifies at landing; `Check Changeset` is not one of the seven required contexts.
- New changeset `20701-import-row-not-null-and-unique-door-answer.md` (`@objectstack/rest` `patch`): every claim is pinned or verified above. The NOT NULL row's `code: 'required'`, `field`, "f is required" (pinned); "it used to fail with the database's own code (`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_NOTNULL` on SQLite) and no `field`" (the flipped pin asserted exactly that on the base); the door's `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with a `required` finding (pinned through `notNullDoor`); "the way it reports a `required` field the engine refuses itself" (the import-integration pin); "no database dialect's code reaches the row" (`DIALECT_CODE`, and (a)); the unique row keeps `code` and `field` and carries "A record with this f already exists" in place of the engine's sentence, "which the create door returns as `developerMessage`" (pinned: `error` equals the door's and is `not.toBe(developerMessage)`); the async job's rows (pinned); "the same mapper as the create door, as it already does for a missing database column" (true); "No key is added" (the exact `ROW_KEYS` pin); "The dry run still previews such rows as `ok`, because it checks the metadata and does not judge `storage.notNull` or uniqueness" (measured by the dev, and consistent with the source: `previewVerdict` asks `validateData`, and `packages/objectql/src` has no read of `notNull` outside a comment). It claims nothing undelivered. Two omissions, neither a false claim: the sandbox-producer and status-passthrough residues in (a), the same omissions item 4's record accepted.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` with `patch` is right under AGENTS.md's changeset rule. Neither limb fires: the file list touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and the claim declares `no`. The accept set does not move: `ImportRowResultSchema`'s key set is unchanged (pinned exact), `code` takes values the row already emits (`required` from the field-level catalog it already speaks for a metadata-required field; `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` already emitted), a driver-dialect code was never contract vocabulary (ADR-0112), so its leaving `code` narrows no declared set, and `error` is prose. No row moves between `ok` and `failed`; the dry run is untouched. A bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never none, and the note carries the migration-free shape a non-breaking changeset needs (no ADR-0087 marker required). The claim's own Clause-② reading (`5920542737`) says the same and the dev re-read it against the real diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `deviations`, each answered:
1. The edit to item 4's pending changeset: confirmed in ①(d) as the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. It is inside the claim's `.changeset/20701-*.md` surface literally, and the correction is required rather than optional, since the sentence would otherwise ship false in the same release. Accepted.
2. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally (two container restarts during turbo builds; correlation, not cause, so not retried on the shared box): `Build Core` and `Type Check · debt ledger` / `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head cover both; their conclusions are below. Accepted.
3. `origin/main` moved to `013f97df93` (three commits: spec docs, cli docs, driver-memory), none touching `packages/rest`, `objectql`, `types`, `metadata-protocol`, `driver-sql` or the `20701` changesets; the branch was not merged and the suite not re-run. AGENTS.md §10's scoped re-check allows it; CI already tests the merge ref (`MERGE_BASE: 013f97df93` in the `Check Changeset` log) and the queue rebuilds again. Accepted.
4. Five files in the shared `issue-20701/` scratch directory were overwritten before this run moved to `issue-20701-item5/`: reads for items already landed, nothing in the repo, and every input a reviewer needs is on GitHub. Accepted.
5. Commit trailers: verified on the one commit `1eada1f134`, the model-free pair (`Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VvcEokUG1tvVxkceYfR5XB` and `Co-authored-by: Claude`), as AGENTS.md requires over the harness reminder; no model identifier in the title, body, changesets or code. Accepted.
6. Worktree and `node_modules` removed after the report posts. Accepted.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, each answered or escalated:
1. **A dry-run preview of a row missing a `storage.notNull` value answers ok/created while the commit fails it (class a, measured at both bases): ESCALATED to the dispatching seat, for triage as a candidate in the card's own family.** It is a different case from the one Ask 2 settled: there the column was missing from an un-migrated environment and the metadata could not know; here the constraint IS in the metadata (`storage: { notNull: true }` on the field), so a metadata-reading validator could judge it with no driver read, and neither of triage's reasons for Ask 2 (the cost of reading the driver's column set on every validate; "an environment that has not been migrated ... is the migration door's to report") applies. It is the card's Path line ("an import preview promises only rows the commit will write"). The layer is not REST: a preview-side NOT NULL check in the import would be the second rule triage forbade (`5897601448`), and the create door has no preview. It is the engine's record validator (`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts`, read through `ObjectQL.validate` / `validateData`), which today judges `required` and reads `storage.notNull` nowhere (grep at the head: no `notNull` in `packages/objectql/src` outside a redaction comment). It needs an ADR-0113 reading before anyone codes it: ADR-0113 D1/D2 keep the write contract (`required`) and the column constraint (`storage.notNull`) deliberately apart, and Q1 names "`storage.notNull` alone" as the engine-populated column cell (audit fields, the tenant column), values the engine fills after validation, so a validator that refused every payload missing a `storage.notNull` value would refuse every insert; the rule would have to judge the post-population record or exempt engine-populated columns. So: `domain:engine`, with a decision (an ADR-0113 amendment or a scoped ruling), which is triage's or the maintainer's call, exactly as Ask 2 was. The dev's class and reach are right; folding it into #20701's family rather than a single-point card is the seat's call. Not a verdict mover.
2. **The door's NOT NULL `hint` tells the caller the schema has drifted and to run `os migrate`, even for a column the metadata declares NOT NULL on purpose (class a, measured on the create door): ESCALATED to the seat to file.** Class: runs but wrong prose (the `code`, `field` and sentence are right; only the remedy is wrong). Reach: every route that answers a driver NOT NULL refusal through `mapDataError`'s not-null branch, `POST /data/:object` and `PATCH /data/:object/:id` measured, plus any `handleRouteError` / `sendThrownError` caller that reaches `classifyDataError` with such an error; not the import row, since `hint` is not copied (the `ROW_KEYS` pin). File: `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`, the `notNull` branch (its `hint` string and the comment "a NOT NULL violation that reaches this far means ... the physical column has drifted from metadata (#2186)", both written before ADR-0113 made `storage.notNull` a declared posture). A fix is prose in that one file: the hint must cover the ADR-0113 case (a field declaring `storage.notNull` without `required`: the column requires the value, provide it or declare `required`) and can name drift only as one possibility, because the mapper sees the error and the object name, not the field map; telling the two apart would need a registry read, a wider change than the card asks. Prime Directive 10: a reproducible, measured defect gets a card; the dev's entry is card-shaped (reach, evidence, dedupe words). Low stakes, as the dev says. Not a verdict mover.
3. `isEngineDuplicateRecordEnvelope` unreachable in practice: answered in ①(c), right; "noted, not filed" is right (no defect, a dead predicate kept for the door-parity docblock). Accepted.
4. The passthrough `field` drop and the sandbox `innerMessage`: answered in ①(a), both are the door's answer; no producer of the first shape reaches the import through the engine (the five envelope exits, verified in `engine.ts`), and the second is item 4's residue class. "Noted, not filed" is right. Accepted.
